people.name: Ziyun Wang
people.bio: Dr. Ziyun Wang is a computational chemist specializing in theoretical catalysis and machine learning. He did his doctoral research at Queen’s University Belfast and the University of Manchester with Prof. Peijun Hu and Prof. Chris Hardacre, then postdoctoral research at Stanford University with Prof. Jens Nørskov and Prof. Thomas Bligaard, and with Prof. Edward Sargent at the University of Toronto. He joined the School of Chemical Sciences at the University of Auckland in 2021, where he is an Associate Professor. He is a Clarivate Highly Cited Researcher and is listed among Stanford’s World’s Top 2% Scientists.

people.name: Yu Mao
people.bio: Dr. Yu Mao earned his Ph.D. in Physical Chemistry from Queen’s University Belfast and his B.E. in Applied Chemistry from East China University of Science and Technology. With a background in theoretical chemistry and heterogeneous catalysis, he is currently focusing on understanding and designing catalysts for electrocatalytic reactions (e.g., CO2RR, OER/ORR) using DFT and MD/AIMD calculations.

people.name: Wensheng Fang
people.bio: Wensheng Fang obtained his PhD degree in 2025 at Huazhong University of Science and Technology (HUST). His current research primarily focuses on the synthesis of functional nanomaterials and the design of devices for electrocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction.

people.name: Yingxin Li
people.bio: Yingxin Li started her undergraduate studies in science at the University of Auckland, majoring in food science. After receiving her Bachelor of Science degree, she then pursued an honors degree, and in August 2022, she graduated with her honors degree in Food Science with first-class honors. She decided to study further and started her PhD in November 2022. Due to uncontrollable circumstances, she switched from food science to chemistry science, taking on the challenge of studying a new path focusing on integrating CO2 reduction with food applications. She joined Dr Ziyun Wang’s group in early 2023.

people.name: Ruihu Lu
people.bio: Ruihu Lu received his master’s degree in the school of Materials Science and Engineering at Wuhan University of Technology. With a background in material science and theoretical computations. He joined the Wang group in 2023 as a Ph.D. student. He is currently focusing on theoretical investigation on CO2 reduction and theoretical-guided experimental catalyst’s discovery for the selective CO2RR towards various carbonous production, including formic acid, ethanol, ethylene et al.

people.name: Xiu Wang
people.bio: Xiu Wang received her M.S. degree from the School of Science, Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics. She is currently under the supervision of Dr. Ziyun Wang for her Ph.D. degree. Her research primarily focuses on unraveling the mechanisms of plasmonic-assisted electrocatalysis in the CO2 reduction reaction.

people.name: Chengyi Zhang
people.focus: Machine learning and DFT for CO₂ reduction
people.bio: Chengyi Zhang received his master’s degree in the Institute of technological science, Wuhan University. He joined the Wang group in 2023 as Ph.D. student. He is investigating the mechanism of CO2RR by machine learning and DFT simulation.

people.name: Xingyu Wang
people.bio: Xingyu Wang received her M.S. degree from the School of Chemistry, Sichuan University. She is currently under the supervision of Dr. Ziyun Wang for her Ph.D. degree. Her research primarily focuses on machine learning in chemistry.

people.name: Mengyao Chang
people.bio: Mengyao Chang earned her M.S. degree in Materials and Chemical Engineering from the Beijing University of Chemical Technology. With a background in synthesizing, modifying, and evaluating inorganic nanomaterials, she now focuses on designing electrocatalyst surfaces to understand the mechanisms of various electrochemical reactions better.

people.name: Mengjiao Li
people.bio: Mengjiao Li received her M.S. degree from the School of Science, Tianjin University. She is currently under the supervision of Dr. Ziyun Wang for her Ph.D. degree. Her research primarily focuses on the advanced catalysts’ design under theory-guided experiments.

people.name: Xingbao Chen
people.focus: CO₂ reduction catalysts and in-situ characterisation
people.bio: Xingbao Chen earned his B.S. in Material Forming and Control Engineering from Hubei University of Technology, Hubei, China, and acquired his M.S. in Material Science and Engineering from Wuhan University of Technology, Hubei, China. He is pursuing his Ph.D. at the University of Auckland under the guidance of Dr. Ziyun Wang and Prof. Paul Kilmartin. He specializes in designing catalysts aimed at enhancing CO2 electrochemical reduction performance and unraveling their mechanisms through meticulous in-situ and ex-situ characterization. He joined Dr. Wang’s group in September 2024.

people.name: Shijia Li
people.bio: Shijia Li received her M.S. degree from the School of Materials Science and Engineering, East China University of Science and Technology. She is currently under the supervision of Dr. Ziyun Wang for her Ph.D. Degree. Her research primarily focuses on designing catalysts for electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction and ammonia synthesis.

people.name: Zhanghao Ren
people.bio: Zhanghao Ren is a member of the Theoretical Catalysis Group working on machine learning.

people.name: Botong Chu
people.bio: Botong Chu joined Wang’s group in 2023. He graduated with a bachelor’s degree in chemistry from Northeast Forestry University. His primary research areas involve using computer-aided engineering (CAE) to simulate electrochemical reactions (e.g., CO2RR, HER, and NO3RR), electrolyzer/battery design, plasma reactor optimization, and computational fluid dynamics. Botong is dedicated to applying simulation calculations to achieve practical technological applications.

people.name: Liwei Zhang
people.bio: Liwei Zhang is a member of the Theoretical Catalysis Group working on machine learning.

people.name: Zhekang Zhao
people.focus: DFT for urea synthesis and CO₂ reduction
people.bio: Zhekang Zhao graduated with a bachelor’s degree in chemistry from Northeast Forestry University in 2025 and is currently pursuing a BSc (Honours) in Chemistry at the University of Auckland. His primary research areas involve using DFT calculations to study urea synthesis and CO2RR.

people.name: Rui Huang
people.bio: Rui Huang obtained his Ph.D. in Energy and Environmental Engineering from Zhejiang University and his bachelor's degree in Energy and Power Engineering from Wuhan University. He currently serves as an Associate Professor at Guizhou University. His research interests lie in the development of biomass-based carbon materials for CO₂ capture and catalytic conversion.

people.name: Siwen Zhang
people.bio: Siwen Zhang is an Assistant Researcher at Liaoning University. He received his Ph.D. from Harbin Institute of Technology. During his doctoral studies, he was awarded a scholarship from the China Scholarship Council, enabling him to spend 18 months as a joint Ph.D. student at the National University of Singapore. His main research interests focus on the fundamental and industrial research of key materials for electrochemical energy storage, including aqueous batteries and sodium-ion batteries. To date, he has published more than 30 SCI-indexed papers as first author or corresponding author in internationally renowned journals such as Advanced Materials, Angewandte Chemie International Edition, and Energy & Environmental Science.

people.name: Bosi Yin
people.bio: Bosi Yin is an associate Professor at the School of Chemistry, Liaoning University, and she is a Master's Supervisor. Her main research interests include aqueous zinc ion battery and other metal ion batteries (Na⁺, Mg²⁺, K⁺), flexible and pliable supercapacitors and intelligent temperature-sensitive aqueous batteries, specifically encompassing the modification of positive electrode materials, optimization of negative electrode materials, and the study of electrolyte additives. Currently, she has published over 40 SCI papers in the field of electrochemical energy storage, with more than 20 as the first author/corresponding author in prestigious international journals such as Energy & Environmental Science, Advanced Materials, Angewandte Chemie, Nano Energy, Carbon Energy, Energy Storage Materials, Small, Nano-Micro Letters, and others. She has an H-index of 25 and one of her papers has been recognized as an ESI Highly Cited Paper (top 1% worldwide). She holds one granted patent and five pending patents, with two achievements successfully transformed into practical applications. As the principal investigator, she has led/participated in five national key laboratory projects, general projects, and other regional funding projects, as well as two enterprise-sponsored projects.

people.name: Tianxiong Liu
people.bio: Tianxiong Liu is a Ph.D. student at Hunan University. He joined the Wang group as a visiting student in October 2025 for a period of two years. His research focuses on integrated CO2 capture and electrocatalytic reduction technologies.

people.name: Zhuo Li
people.bio: Zhuo Li obtained his master’s degree from Harbin Engineering University, where he is currently pursuing his Ph.D. In October 2024, he joined Professor Ziyun Wang’s research group at the University of Auckland as a joint Ph.D. His current research focuses on aqueous secondary batteries, zinc anode protection, and lithium metal batteries, with theoretical calculations and simulations. His research interests primarily center on the microscopic behavior and regulation of zinc at aqueous zinc anode interfaces. He has published seven peer-reviewed papers as the first author, with an i-index of 11.

people.name: Jingjing Shi
people.bio: Jingjing Shi is a Ph.D. candidate at the Institute of Chemical Industry of Forest Products, Chinese Academy of Forestry, who joined Wang’s research team as a visiting scholar in January 2026. His primary research focus lies in the thermocatalytic and electrocatalytic conversion of lignin for the production of high-calorific-value liquid fuels and high-value chemicals.

people.name: Yuhang Han
people.bio: Yuhang Han is a Ph.D. student at Northeast Forestry University. In January 2026, he joined Professor Ziyun Wang’s research group at the University of Auckland as a joint Ph.D. student for a period of two years. His research primarily centers on flexible/stretchable electrode materials and their applications in electrochemical CO2 reduction. He is dedicated to enhancing carbon capture and conversion efficiency by engineering the microenvironment of flexible electrocatalysts.

people.name: Jiexin Zhu
people.bio: Jiexin Zhu is currently a postdoctoral fellow at Prof. David Sinton/Prof. Ted Sargent's group at the University of Toronto. He was a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Auckland. He earned his Ph.D. in Materials Science and Engineering from Wuhan University of Technology in 2023. With a background in electrochemistry, electrocatalytic, low-dimensional materials, and in-situ characterizations, he is currently focusing on materials discovery and system optimal for electrocatalytic system, including CO₂ reduction, nitrate reduction, and water splitting.

people.name: Yuying Zhao
people.bio: Yuying Zhao received her Ph.D. at the Institute of Chemical Industry of Forest Products, Chinese Academy of Forestry, in 2024. She studied as a visiting student in the Wang group during 2023-2024. She is now working at Qilu University of Technology. Her current research focused on the preparation of biomass-based carbon materials and the study of their electrocatalytic performance in the electrochemical CO₂RR and 4e⁻/2e⁻ ORR.

people.name: Ziyi Li
people.bio: Ziyi Li received her Ph.D. at Hunan University in 2024. She studied as a visiting student in the Wang group during 2023.11-2024.05. She is now working at Changsha University of Science and Technology. Her research mainly focused on photocatalytic CO₂ reduction and CO₂ utilization.

people.name: Hang Xu
people.bio: Hang Xu is a professor at the School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering at Henan University of Science and Technology (HAUST). He joined the Wang group in August 2023 as a visiting scholar for one year, supported by the China Scholarship Council (CSC). His research interests focus on the oxidation desulfurization process.

people.name: Zihao Jiao
people.bio: Zihao Jiao is a Ph.D. student at the State Key Laboratory of Multi-phase Flow in Power Engineering at Xi'an Jiaotong University (XJTU). He joined the Wang group in September 2023 as a one-year visiting student. His research centers on the theoretical investigation of catalytic mechanisms for the photo-electrocatalytic reduction of CO₂. This involves utilizing Density Functional Theory (DFT) to interpret experimental reaction mechanisms and exploring the synergistic mechanisms of Cu-based alloy catalysts through a combination of DFT and Machine Learning (ML).

people.name: Yan Liu
people.bio: Yan Liu earned her Master of Chemistry from the University of Auckland with First-Class Honors. She is currently dedicated to understanding and designing catalysts for various electrochemical reactions using Density Functional Theory(DFT) simulations. Her research involves performing DFT calculations of heterogeneous catalytic reactions, focusing on screening and designing catalysts, including metals, oxides, and two-dimensional materials. The research comprehensively covers reaction mechanisms, catalytic activity, structure-activity relationships, and activity regulation. By combining experimental results with DFT calculations, Yan systematically explores critical electrochemical reactions (e.g., HER, OER, ORR, CO₂RR, NO₃RR, and HMFOR). Yan joined the Dr. Wang's group in February 2023. Congratulations her Ph.D. journey to National University of Singapore.

people.name: Junyao Wu
people.bio: Junyao Wu earned her M.S. and B.S. in Environmental Science and Engineering from China University of Geosciences, Beijing. She is currently pursuing her Ph.D. at the University of Auckland, where she is co-supervised by Prof. Wei Gao (FRSNZ, FEngNZ, ONZOM) and Dr. Ziyun Wang. Her research focuses on developing computational catalysis for environmental materials design and water treatment technologies, such as PFAS removal. She joined Dr. Wang's group in May 2022.

people.name: Jiajian Guan
people.bio: Jiajian Guan received his B.S. and M.S. degrees in Materials Physics and Chemistry from Southwest University, China. He is currently working as a PhD candidate in Wang's group. His research interests include but are not limited to the thermodynamics of ion beams and electron beam-assisted phase engineering of nanomaterials (PEN).

people.name: Kai Sun
people.bio: Kai Sun earned his Ph.D. in Chemistry from Beijing University of Chemical Technology, with a background in inorganic synthetic chemistry and electrochemistry. He is now focusing on single-atom catalysts and inorganic crystal catalysts for electrocatalysis.

people.name: Can Li
people.bio: Can Li is an associate professor at the College of Optical and Electronic Technology at China Jiliang University. In June 2024, he joined the Wang group as a visiting scholar for five months. His research interests focus on the design of active centers in photo- and electro-catalysts, utilizing both experimental methods and DFT simulations.

people.name: Dawei Jiang
people.bio: Dawei Jiang is an associate professor at the College of Chemistry, Chemical Engineering and Resource Utilization, Northeast Forestry University. He joined the Wang’s group in April 2024 as a visiting scholar for one year, supported by the China Scholarship Council (CSC). His research interests focus on interface science of composite materials, flameresistant material and flexible strain sensing material.

people.name: Chanthip Wangphon
people.bio: Chanthip Wangphon earned her B.S. in Industrial Chemistry from King Mongkut’s Institute of Technology Ladkrabang in Bangkok, Thailand. She is currently pursuing her Ph.D. at Chulalongkorn University under the supervision of Assoc. Prof. Supareak Praserthdam, with Dr. Tinnakorn Saelee serving as co-supervisor. Her research focuses on computational catalysis, particularly focusing on high-entropy alloy (HEA) catalysts for NOx reduction in Passive NH3-SCR processes. From January 2025 to May 2025, she joined Dr. Wang’s group as a visiting student.

people.name: Jianping Sun
people.bio: Jianping Sun is a professor at the School of Resources, Environment and Materials Guangxi University. He joined the Wang’s group in Jan. 2025 as a visiting scholar for half a year, supported by the China Scholarship Council (CSC). His research interests focus on optimization design of biomass materials based on machine learning, biobased intelligent wearable sensing materials.

people.name: Yiming Zou
people.bio: Yiming Zou joined Wang's group in 2024. He graduated with a bachelor's degree in chemistry from Northeast Forestry University.

people.name: Yang Wang
people.bio: Yang Wang is a Ph.D. student at Xi’an Jiaotong University. She joined the Wang group as a visiting student from 2025 to 2026 for one year, supported by the China Scholarship Council (CSC). Her research centers on the electrochemical reduction of CO2.

people.name: Wenqing Chu
people.bio: Wenqing Chu earned his B.E. from Zhejiang University and is currently pursuing a Ph.D. in the Department of Energy and Power Engineering at Tsinghua University. Her research focuses on the design of Cu-based catalysts for electrochemical CO₂ reduction (CO₂RR) and on mechanistic understanding of activity and selectivity, aiming to correlate catalyst structure with reaction intermediates and C–C coupling pathways.

people.name: Kunpeng Gao
people.bio: Kunpeng Gao earned his Master of Science in Chemistry from the University of Auckland, and Bachelor's degree in Chemistry from Northeast Forestry University. He joined the research group in 2025, and his research currently focuses on advancing the performance and stability of aqueous zinc-ion batteries.
